**Folding Mixed-Integer Linear Programs and Reflection Symmetries**

*Rolf van der Hulst*

70 pp, 24 sections.

**Abstract.** For mixed-integer linear programming and linear programming it is well known that symmetries can have a negative impact on the performance of branch- and-bound and linear optimization algorithms. A common strategy to handle symmetries in linear programs is to reduce the dimension of the linear program by aggregating symmetric variables and solving a linear program of reduced dimen- sion. In their work Dimension Reduction via Color Refinement (DRCR), Grohe, Kersting, Mladenov and Selman show that it is sufficient to run a fast color refinement algorithm to detect permutation symmetries and reduce the dimen- sion of the linear program. We extend DRCR in two directions. First, we show that DRCR can be extended to reflection symmetries, which generalize permuta- tion symmetries.

**Outline.** Front matter; Introduction; Contribution; Outline; Dimension Reduction via Color Refinement; Equitable partitions and fractional automorphi; Dimension Reduction of a Linear Program; Extending DRCR to reflection symmetries; Centering the linear program; Split reformulations of linear programs; Equitable partitions of split reformulations; Reducing the split reformulation; Choosing the affine offset; Comparison with reflection symmetries; Detecting reflection reductions; Dimension Reduction for Mixed-Integer Linear P; Affine TU decompositions for mixed-integer lin; Example: Generalized Assignment problem
